_note: Chapter 2 beats. The finale is a five-step sequence (design-document §6) delivered through this system rather than a bespoke mechanic. Steps gate on Apocrypha progress rather than ticks, so a player who never studies the Apocrypha reaches the takeover without ever attempting severance — and the Presidium takes over anyway.

beats._note: Walk into the Board meeting where the death is announced and perform shock convincingly for people who have no idea. A natural tutorial for revelation staging before the Nexus has sent a single directive — the player learns to lie about something they did, which is the whole chapter in one scene.
The Board installs the Chair as interim Mayor, using the succession clause written at founding. Public Mayor, Chair of the Board, and the Nexus's extended arm, all at once.
Finale step 1. Gated behind Apocrypha investigation progress — the Chair theorises the Nexus can be traced, jammed or seized.

Finale step 2. dir-05 breaks pattern and someone is on the other end — a handler assigned to this Shaft, themselves a node in something larger. Characterisation is an open thread (narrative-spine §Open).

Finale step 3. The Chair decides which board members to bring into confidence — saying aloud what they have hidden all chapter, to people who could report them. Recruiting the engineering rep grants technical muscle or ends the attempt on the spot; see members.json coalitionRisk.

Finale step 4. The Presidium does not negotiate — it demonstrates. The clean water and scrubbed air the Shaft believed it produced have been supplied from outside all along. Fires the catalyst-interruption dilemma. Pays off a detail the player has been staring at for twenty hours.

Finale step 5. The Presidium enters physically through the hidden passage foreshadowed in doc-lower-schematic. Aftermath: the population never learns, the Board survives as coerced insiders, the Chair is eliminated, and the mole is installed as the new Mayor and Chair. board.revealMole targets lowest-doubt — the member who seemed safest.
A player who never attempts severance still reaches the ending. Judged unreliable for a different reason, or simply no longer needed — the takeover was never contingent on the Chair's defiance.
